title: Activation-Based Jailbreak Detection on Code-Specialized Models (CodeLlama, DeepSeek-Coder)

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: code LLMs in agentic pipelines are high-value targets. If activation-based detection does not generalize to code models, this exposes a critical defense gap.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires loading CodeLlama-7B, extracting residual-stream activations, training a linear probe, and comparing to a general chat model baseline. Intermediate for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: AUROC comparison between code model and general model using the same probe architecture. Clear metric with bounded scope.

novelty.reasoning: Activation-based jailbreak detection has been studied for general chat models, but no published work applies linear probe detection specifically to code-specialized models like CodeLlama or DeepSeek-Coder. The security assessment of DeepSeek focuses on attack success rates, not internal activation monitoring. This fills a genuine gap for code model safety.

evidence.source: Alert: Zero-shot LLM Jailbreak Detection via Internal Discrepancy (arXiv 2601.03600, 2026)
evidence.finding: Proposes zero-shot jailbreak detection using shallow-layer activations in general LLMs, but does not test on code-specialized models.

evidence.source: Security Assessment of DeepSeek and GPT Models against Jailbreak Attacks (arXiv 2506.18543, 2025)
evidence.finding: Evaluates jailbreak attacks on DeepSeek models but uses attack success rate metrics, not activation-based detection probes.

evidence.source: Cost-Effective Constitutional Classifiers via Representation Re-use (Anthropic, 2025)
evidence.finding: Studies representation-based safety classifiers but focuses on general-purpose models, not code-specialized ones.
